feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: it shows clear progression, relevant public-sector scope, and solid technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership scope across web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and budget management.  
- Good use of scale indicators and credibility signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership through a blend of strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and project descriptions; consolidate overlapping sections to improve scannability and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope, especially for consulting and earlier roles: e.g., engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), inconsistent list punctuation, and title casing. No obvious misspellings; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstraction: replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast “Leads” to first-person implied summary style: “Experienced in leading” or “Leads” is fine, but keep tense/style consistent with the rest of the CV.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, digital governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Built and scaled enterprise platforms supporting 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ internal publishers, with expertise spanning editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; use the intro to add scale/results rather than restate positioning.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Keep the most distinctive, current strengths: AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions; use parallel noun phrases throughout.
- Consider reducing to 6–7 items for sharper scanning and less repetition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Topline Skills and Work Experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet for easier scanning.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built” and “Developed” with stronger, more differentiated language: “Launched,” “Architected,” “Produced,” “Led.”
- Tighten wording and standardize style: use “AI-enabled” consistently, spell out “10 x 20-foot” or use “10-by-20-foot,” and keep parallel structure across all entries.
- Where possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker to each project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current/future work experience bullets; keep this section shorter and more outcome-focused to avoid repetition.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here and helps broaden the portfolio beyond what’s already covered elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground outcomes/ownership, and avoid repeating project details already covered in Recent Projects.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper value statement: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Improved,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, engagement or conversion lifts.
- Suggested phrasing: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current bullets overlap with the footer projects (AI search, microsites, anniversary campaign/toolkits); keep this entry focused on role-level ownership and outcomes, not project specifics.
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” echoes prior NACo roles; only keep if you can show a new or higher-level contribution.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management language is reduced to avoid overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact wins first: website migration, analytics infrastructure, video studio, governance/operations.
- Tighten channel bullet to focus on ownership + scale, e.g., “Oversaw enterprise email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and other public-sector stakeholders.” Add growth, engagement, or efficiency metrics if available.
- Make outcomes explicit where possible: website redesign “improved publishing for 50+ contributors,” analytics stack “standardized executive reporting,” governance “reduced bottlenecks/increased consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper verbs and any measurable growth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and quantify views, cadence, or engagement if available.
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership: “Standardized digital publishing workflows and cross-team editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical, not governance-heavy.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope and strategic strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-functional digital leadership” if you want to stress team/stakeholder management.
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier such as “for complex, high-volume organizations” to reinforce scale.
- Keep terms parallel in structure; avoid mixing broad functions (“strategy”) with tactical activities (“planning”) unless consistently framed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. It should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, impact-oriented capabilities: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older tools here unless central to target roles; keep SharePoint/Power Pages only if the job requires them.
- Remove “jQuery” from Topline Skills; it reads dated and is better left in Technical + IT if needed.
- If space allows, make it outcome-linked: “Drupal platform delivery and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation • API and workflow integration • AI-enabled search and structured content systems”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost line for line.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to an outcomes-oriented line, e.g.:
  “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards” or “executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “KPI design” to “measurement framework design” if you want a more senior, strategic tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent work, such as supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack in multiple sections; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and higher-value production capabilities rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production systems
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the studio/buildout experience.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event production” for tighter phrasing and less repetition.
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of generic terms: “recurring advocacy programming” or “conference/event broadcast support.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and general video production are already evidenced in NACo roles, so this section should stay concise and specialized.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of only names: “Drupal 9/10” or “SharePoint Online” if accurate.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels lighter than the rest and may dilute seniority.
- Keep platform naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use this section for systems only, not broader capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates Topline Skills [2] almost exactly; consider removing one section or making this one more technical/version-specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag management integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Consider replacing older/basic labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) with stronger phrasing like “front-end development” if space is tight.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation” or “deployment/workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Data, Analytics & Optimization unless you specifically used it for implementation-heavy tagging architecture.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more strategic by grouping tools by function and emphasizing the platforms most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a flat list: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general tools if you need space for stronger technical items elsewhere; this section is strongest when it signals systems-building, not basic workplace familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams can feel generic unless framed as collaboration platforms rather than standout technical skills.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to signal level of ownership or relevance. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/usage context in brief: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (newsletter, member communications, campaign email)
- Keep only platforms you directly used/administered; if one was peripheral, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader multi-channel competencies, so make this item explicitly email/member-platform oriented.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Tighten it to emphasize tools over generic capabilities and align with the stronger, recent NACo impact already shown.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation reporting
- Replace generic terms like “Dashboarding” and “A/B testing” with more specific, resume-ready phrasing tied to execution or reporting.
- If accurate, swap in a more concrete tool for SEO (e.g., Google Search Console, SEMrush) rather than listing “SEO” as a broad discipline.
- Keep ordering by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this version tools-only.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” may feel under-supported unless referenced elsewhere in work experience or projects.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, e.g.: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping improve publishing workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: number/frequency of livestreams, weekly videos produced, size/timing of website refresh, or team supported.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables like “livestreams, weekly advocacy videos, and web content.”
- End with light leadership language: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” rather than overstating management.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early producing the series if true.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is echoed in later roles; keep this item more hands-on and production-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later multimedia/digital leadership roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer contribution: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry focused on research/program support and the podcast origin story, not broader digital operations that are covered in later NACo roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production” overlaps with later video/studio roles; keep this item lighter on generic production language.
- Avoid repeating web/email/social responsibilities here, since those become central in later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it more tool-focused and specific to software proficiency, not production responsibilities.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to: “Creative Software” or “Multimedia Editing Tools”
- Replace with tighter, software-led phrasing: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If true, add level/scope instead of broad functions: “Video editing • Audio cleanup/mixing • Graphic asset creation” or “Studio video post-production • Podcast audio editing”
- Keep only tools here; move workflow terms to competencies if needed

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates “Livestreaming • PTZ camera systems • Studio operations • Hybrid and virtual event production”
- “Podcast production” is already evidenced in work experience; if kept, make it narrower: “Podcast editing” or “Podcast post-production”
